core_obligations: The refined covering (proof lines 9519-9522): the author chooses an index at which the given element of the colimit is represented, forms the fibre products of the members of the given finite covering over that representative, and observes that they form a finite covering.

Separation of the two sections (proof lines 9523-9533): the sheaf condition gives an inclusion of values into the product over the refined covering, and the commutation of filtered colimits with finite limits makes the induced comparison map injective, so some member of the refined covering already separates the two sections.

The refinement (proof lines 9534-9543): the author adjoins the chosen indices to the original index set, orders them suitably, records that the transition maps are left unspecified, and concludes both that the two sections remain distinct and that the given element restricts through the chosen member of the covering.
proof_roadmap: Choose an index representing the given element and take fibre products with the covering.
Use the sheaf condition and commutation of filtered colimits with finite limits to separate the sections.
Adjoin the chosen indices and read off the required refinement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a system defining a point can be refined so that two distinct sections remain distinct and a given element of the colimit becomes liftable through a member of a prescribed finite covering (statement lines 9502-9516). The proof is a complete construction: an index representing the given element is chosen and the members of the covering are pulled back to it, giving a finite covering (proof lines 9519-9522); the sheaf condition together with the commutation of filtered colimits with finite limits shows that two sections are already separated by one member (proof lines 9523-9533); and adjoining the chosen indices to the original system with a suitable order produces the required refinement, with the author recording that the transition maps are left unspecified (proof lines 9534-9543). The non-formal content is the construction of the refinement. The claim is H2: a construction with the routine omission noted.
